beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Riley shows up rattled, phone still in her hand.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "The label restructured overnight. The whole deal my partner and I built the last two months around — gone, this morning, no warning."

options.text: That's a real shock — how are you doing right now?
Is that actually a bad thing?

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "I keep replaying every conversation, trying to find where the warning sign was that I missed."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You turn over the top card.

options.text: There might not have been a sign — some things were unstable long before they showed it.
There's always a sign, you just weren't paying attention.
This card has nothing to do with sudden change.

elaboration: Sudden, unexpected change — and what falls apart was usually already unstable; the collapse just finally makes it visible.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "So was any of it even real, or was I building on nothing this whole time?"

options.text: It was real enough while it stood — the point now is knowing how you fall, not whether you fell.
None of it was real, you wasted two months.
How you fall doesn't matter, only whether you fell.

elaboration: The point isn't the falling — it's knowing how to fall. Resisting the change costs more than actually flowing with it.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "...Okay. I guess I'd rather learn how to land than spend a week pretending the ground didn't move."
